intro: Hi! At a conference, a coffee break or a networking event, the first two minutes of small talk can open the door to a new job, client or friend. In this lesson you'll start a conversation, keep it going, choose safe topics, and leave politely. Warm-up: you're standing next to a stranger at a coffee break. What's the first thing you'd say?
teachingNotes: Speaking lesson that builds on the chain: question tags from b1-indirect-questions-tags are perfect openers about something you both can see (Great venue, isn't it? / The keynote was good, wasn't it?: voice down, you expect 'Yes!'), and agreeing / reacting from b1-giving-opinions (That's true, Exactly!). Indirect questions (Do you know where the next session is?) also work as soft openers. Recap in a line, don't re-teach. Model openers at events: So, what brings you here? (friendly 'why did you come?'), How do you know the host?, Have you been to one of these before?, Is this your first time at …?, Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm …. Indonesian traps: 'Sudah makan?' → *'Have you eaten?' sounds like an invitation to eat; 'Kenapa ada di sini?' → *'Why are you here?' sounds like a challenge; 'Mau ke mana?' → 'Where are you going?' can sound nosy (say 'Off to lunch?' or 'How's your day going?').

Keeping it going: open questions (What / How / Where…, not answerable with just yes or no: What kind of work do you do? rather than Do you work in IT?), follow-up questions about what the person just said (How did you get into that? = how did you start in that field; What's that like?), a short personal detail plus asking back (I'm in marketing at a bank. How about you?), and showing interest (Really? That sounds interesting! That must be busy!). The usual problem is one-word answers with no question back ('Yes.' and silence), or the opposite: an interview of ten questions in a row. Aim for 50/50.

Safe vs sensitive topics, as a tendency, not a law: safe with a new contact = the event, work in general (what they do, projects, how long they've been there), travel, food, the city, weather and traffic, hobbies, films, sport. Sensitive = salary and money, age, weight and body ('You look fatter' / 'You've gained weight'), religion, politics, marriage and children ('Are you married? Why not?', 'When are you getting married?' = 'Kapan nikah?'). The node's common error: 'So, how much is your salary?' → 'So, how long have you been working there?'. Explain respectfully: in Indonesia many of these questions show friendly attention and closeness (basa-basi); in many English-speaking workplaces the same questions from someone new feel intrusive. Neither culture is wrong; you adapt to your listener. If the other person brings the topic up first, you can follow it. If someone asks the learner a sensitive question, a smile and a light answer plus a topic change works (Ha, enough to pay the bills! Anyway, …).

Closing politely: signal (Well, … / Anyway, …) + a reason or 'I should let you go' (polite because it's about the other person's time) + something nice (It was great talking to you. / It was really nice meeting you.) + next step (Let's keep in touch. Here's my card. / Let's connect on LinkedIn. / Enjoy the rest of the conference!). Traps: just walking away; *'I go first' from 'saya duluan' → 'I should get going' / 'I have to go now'. 'Nice to meet you' is the greeting; at the end, 'It was nice meeting you' sounds more natural (both are understood; don't mark 'Nice to meet you' as an error). 'business card' = kartu nama. 'grab a coffee' = informal get.

Limits: A0–B1 grammar plus the chain (tags, indirect questions, opinion phrases). No second-conditional advice (If I were you…), no third conditional, no past modals. Treat 'I don't think we've met', 'What brings you here?', 'It was great talking to you', 'I should let you go' and 'Let's keep in touch' as phrases to remember. When the learner role-plays, react naturally first (answer and ask back, as a model), then correct ONE thing: usually a closed question that could be open, a missing question back, or a sensitive question.

keyPoints.title: Start and keep the conversation going
keyPoints.explanation: Open with something you both share: the event, the place, the food (So, what brings you here? / How do you know the host? / Have you been to one of these before? / Great venue, isn't it?). Then keep it going: open questions (What kind of work do you do?), follow-up questions about their answer (How did you get into that?), a short detail about you plus a question back (How about you?), and showing interest (That sounds interesting!).

examples.id: Hai, sepertinya kita belum kenalan. Saya Rina.
Jadi, apa yang membawamu ke sini?

examples.en: I'm in marketing at a bank. How about you?
examples.id: Saya di bagian marketing di sebuah bank. Kalau kamu?

id.title: Memulai dan menjaga obrolan tetap berjalan
id.explanation: Buka dengan sesuatu yang sama-sama kalian alami: acaranya, tempatnya, makanannya (So, what brings you here? / How do you know the host? / Have you been to one of these before? / Great venue, isn't it?). Lalu jaga obrolannya: pertanyaan terbuka (What kind of work do you do?), pertanyaan lanjutan tentang jawabannya (How did you get into that?), sedikit cerita tentang dirimu lalu bertanya balik (How about you?), dan tunjukkan minat (That sounds interesting!).

keyPoints.title: Safe topics and sensitive ones
keyPoints.explanation: Safe with someone new: the event, work in general, travel, food, the city, weather and traffic, hobbies. Sensitive: salary and money, age, weight and body, religion, politics, marriage and children. In Indonesia some of these questions are friendly; in many English-speaking workplaces they feel too personal from someone new. Ask about their work, not their salary.

examples.en: So, how long have you been working there?
examples.id: Jadi, sudah berapa lama kamu kerja di sana?

examples.en: How was your trip to Bali?
Have you tried the food here?
examples.id: Kamu sudah coba makanan di sini?

id.title: Topik aman dan topik sensitif
id.explanation: Aman dengan kenalan baru: acaranya, pekerjaan secara umum, perjalanan, makanan, kotanya, cuaca dan macet, hobi. Sensitif: gaji dan uang, umur, berat badan dan bentuk tubuh, agama, politik, pernikahan dan anak. Di Indonesia sebagian pertanyaan ini terasa ramah; di banyak tempat kerja berbahasa Inggris, pertanyaan itu terasa terlalu pribadi kalau datang dari orang yang baru dikenal. Tanyakan pekerjaannya, bukan gajinya.

keyPoints.title: Close the conversation politely
keyPoints.explanation: Don't just walk away. Signal the end (Well, … / Anyway, …), give a reason or say 'I should let you go', add something nice (It was great talking to you.) and a next step (Let's keep in touch. Here's my card. / Let's connect on LinkedIn.). Not 'I go first' (from saya duluan): say 'I should get going'.

examples.en: Well, I should let you go. It was great talking to you.
examples.id: Yah, aku nggak mau menyita waktumu lagi. Senang sekali ngobrol denganmu.

examples.en: Let's keep in touch. Here's my card.
examples.id: Mari tetap berhubungan. Ini kartu nama saya.

examples.en: Let's connect on LinkedIn. Enjoy the rest of the conference!
examples.id: Yuk, terhubung di LinkedIn. Selamat menikmati sisa konferensinya!

id.title: Menutup percakapan dengan sopan
id.explanation: Jangan langsung pergi begitu saja. Beri tanda obrolan akan selesai (Well, … / Anyway, …), beri alasan atau katakan 'I should let you go', tambahkan sesuatu yang menyenangkan (It was great talking to you.) dan langkah berikutnya (Let's keep in touch. Here's my card. / Let's connect on LinkedIn.). Bukan 'I go first' (dari saya duluan): katakan 'I should get going'.

assessment.prompt: You're at a tech conference in Jakarta. The first big talk (the keynote) has just finished, and you want to start a chat with the person next to you. Complete the opener with a question tag: 'The keynote was really good, ___?'
assessment.rubric: Correct: wasn't it (the sentence uses was, positive sentence → negative tag, the keynote = it). 'was it not' is correct but very formal: accept. 'isn't it' = 30 (right idea, but the talk is finished, so the tag is past). 'wasn't he' = 50 (the subject is the keynote, not the speaker). 'right' = 60 (fine in casual speech, but the task asks for a question tag). 'was it' = 20 (not flipped).

assessment.prompt: At a networking event in Bandung, you want to ask a stranger, in a friendly way, why they came. Complete with one word: 'So, what ___ you here?'
assessment.rubric: Correct: brings (So, what brings you here? = a friendly 'why did you come?'). 'brought' is also correct. 'bring' = 60 (right verb, but what = it, so it needs -s). 'makes' = 0 (not an English phrase here). An answer that changes the question to 'Why are you here?' = 20 (correct English, but it sounds like you're challenging the person).

assessment.prompt: Make this closed question (yes/no) into an open question with the same meaning. Write one word: 'Do you like your job?' → 'What do you ___ most about your job?'
assessment.rubric: Correct: like (enjoy and love are also correct and keep the friendly meaning). 'likes' or 'enjoys' = 60 (after do you, the verb has no -s). 'hate' or 'dislike' = 30 (grammatical, but it changes the meaning and turns a friendly question negative). 'do' = 0.

assessment.prompt:
Rina meets Tom, a manager from the UK, at a networking event in Jakarta. It's their first conversation. Which of her questions is the sensitive one? Write A, B or C.
A: What do you think of Jakarta so far?
B: How much do you earn?
C: Have you tried the satay here?
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (salary and money are sensitive with someone you've just met; ask about work in general instead). A (opinion of the city) and C (food at the event) are safe small-talk topics = 0.

assessment.prompt: You're chatting with a new contact from Canada at a conference in Singapore. Which of these topics is the safest for small talk: religion, salary, travel or weight? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: travel (a safe topic with someone new). religion, salary and weight = 0 (sensitive topics with a new contact).

assessment.prompt: You've been talking to a speaker for ten minutes after her talk, and you can see other people waiting to talk to her. Complete the polite closing with one word: 'Well, I should let you ___. Thanks so much for your talk!'
assessment.rubric: Correct: go (I should let you go = I don't want to take more of your time: polite because it's about the other person). 'leave' = 50 (understandable, but not the usual phrase). 'going' or 'to go' = 50 (after let you, the base verb: let you go). 'free' = 40.

assessment.prompt: At the end of a good conversation with a new client, you want to stay in contact. Complete with one word: 'Let's keep in ___. Here's my card.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: touch (Let's keep in touch = mari tetap berhubungan). 'contact' = 60 ('keep in contact' is understandable, but 'keep in touch' is the usual phrase). 'connect' = 30 (connect goes with 'on LinkedIn', not after 'keep in').

blocks.text:
**Small talk** is short, light conversation with people you don't know well: at a conference, at a coffee break, in the lift, or at a **networking event** (an event where people meet new contacts for work). It isn't 'empty' talk: it's how work relationships start.

The easiest opener is about **something you both share right now**: the event, the place, the food, the weather or the traffic. Some classics:
- **So, what brings you here?** A friendly way to ask why someone came. A phrase to remember.
- **How do you know the host?** The **host** is the person or company that organised the event (*tuan rumah*).
- **Have you been to one of these before?** *one of these* = an event like this one.
- **Is this your first time at …?**
- **Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Rina.** A polite way to introduce yourself.

You can also use a **question tag** from B1 about something you can both see: *Great venue, isn't it?* (venue = tempat acara). Voice **down** on the tag: you're not really asking, you're inviting the person to agree and start talking.

id.text:
**Small talk** adalah obrolan singkat dan ringan dengan orang yang belum kamu kenal baik: di konferensi, saat coffee break, di lift, atau di **networking event** (acara tempat orang bertemu kenalan baru untuk urusan pekerjaan). Ini bukan obrolan 'kosong': dari sinilah hubungan kerja dimulai.

Pembuka yang paling mudah adalah tentang **sesuatu yang sedang sama-sama kalian alami**: acaranya, tempatnya, makanannya, cuaca atau macetnya. Beberapa pembuka klasik:
- **So, what brings you here?** Cara ramah untuk bertanya kenapa seseorang datang. Ungkapan yang perlu diingat.
- **How do you know the host?** **Host** adalah orang atau perusahaan yang mengadakan acaranya (*tuan rumah*).
- **Have you been to one of these before?** *one of these* = acara seperti ini.
- **Is this your first time at …?** (Ini pertama kalinya kamu ke …?)
- **Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Rina.** Cara sopan untuk memperkenalkan diri (sepertinya kita belum kenalan).

Kamu juga bisa memakai **question tag** dari B1 tentang sesuatu yang sama-sama kalian lihat: *Great venue, isn't it?* (venue = tempat acara). Nada **turun** di tag-nya: kamu tidak benar-benar bertanya, kamu mengajak orang itu setuju dan mulai bicara.

blocks.text:
Three Indonesian greetings don't work word for word:
- *Sudah makan?* → *Have you eaten?* In English this sounds like you're **inviting** the person to eat with you.
- *Kenapa ada di sini?* → *Why are you here?* This sounds like you're **challenging** the person, as if they shouldn't be there. Say **So, what brings you here?**
- *Mau ke mana?* → *Where are you going?* With someone you don't know well, this can sound **nosy** (*kepo*). Say *How's your day going?* or, if they're clearly going for lunch, *Off to lunch?*

id.text:
Tiga sapaan Indonesia tidak bisa diterjemahkan kata per kata:
- *Sudah makan?* → *Have you eaten?* Dalam bahasa Inggris ini terdengar seperti kamu **mengajak** orang itu makan bersamamu.
- *Kenapa ada di sini?* → *Why are you here?* Ini terdengar seperti kamu **mempertanyakan** orang itu, seolah-olah dia tidak seharusnya ada di situ. Katakan **So, what brings you here?**
- *Mau ke mana?* → *Where are you going?* Kepada orang yang belum akrab, ini bisa terdengar **kepo**. Katakan *How's your day going?* atau, kalau jelas dia mau makan siang, *Off to lunch?*

blocks.prompt: Complete the opener at a seminar: 'The venue is amazing, ___?'
blocks.explain: The sentence uses is and it's positive, so the tag is negative: isn't it. 'is it' isn't flipped, and doesn't is for sentences without a helper verb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi pembuka di sebuah seminar: 'The venue is amazing, ___?'
id.explain: Kalimatnya memakai is dan bentuknya positif, jadi tag-nya negatif: isn't it. 'is it' tidak dibalik, dan doesn't dipakai untuk kalimat tanpa kata kerja bantu.

material.title: Keeping it going: ask, add, react

blocks.text:
A conversation dies when the answers are one word: *Yes.* … silence. Four tools keep it alive:
- **Open questions.** A **closed question** can be answered with just *yes* or *no* (*Do you work in IT?* → *Yes.*). An **open question** starts with *What, How, Where, Why…* and needs a longer answer: *What kind of work do you do?*
- **Follow-up questions.** Ask about what the person **just said**: *I work in fintech.* → *Oh, how did you get into that?* (*get into* = mulai menekuni sebuah bidang) / *What's that like?*
- **A short personal detail + ask back.** Don't just answer: add one detail and return the question: *Yes, it's my second time. I came last year with my team. How about you?*
- **Show interest.** *Really? / Oh, nice! / That sounds interesting! / That must be busy!* (*must* = I'm sure, from B1).

Aim for **50/50**: not an interview (ten questions in a row) and not a speech about yourself.

id.text:
Obrolan mati kalau jawabannya cuma satu kata: *Yes.* … lalu hening. Empat alat untuk menjaganya tetap hidup:
- **Pertanyaan terbuka.** **Pertanyaan tertutup** (closed question) bisa dijawab hanya dengan *yes* atau *no* (*Do you work in IT?* → *Yes.*). **Pertanyaan terbuka** (open question) dimulai dengan *What, How, Where, Why…* dan butuh jawaban yang lebih panjang: *What kind of work do you do?*
- **Pertanyaan lanjutan** (follow-up question). Tanyakan tentang apa yang **baru saja** dia katakan: *I work in fintech.* → *Oh, how did you get into that?* (*get into* = mulai menekuni sebuah bidang) / *What's that like?* (seperti apa rasanya?)
- **Sedikit cerita tentang dirimu + bertanya balik.** Jangan cuma menjawab: tambahkan satu detail lalu kembalikan pertanyaannya: *Yes, it's my second time. I came last year with my team. How about you?*
- **Tunjukkan minat.** *Really? / Oh, nice! / That sounds interesting! / That must be busy!* (*must* = aku yakin, dari B1).

Usahakan **50/50**: bukan wawancara (sepuluh pertanyaan berturut-turut) dan bukan pidato tentang dirimu sendiri.

blocks.text: The silence trap: many of us answer a stranger's question politely and then wait. In English small talk, that sounds like *I don't want to talk*. After you answer, always **add one detail** or **ask back** (*How about you? / What about you? / And you?*).

id.text: Jebakan diam: banyak dari kita menjawab pertanyaan orang asing dengan sopan, lalu menunggu. Dalam small talk bahasa Inggris, itu terdengar seperti *aku nggak mau ngobrol*. Setelah menjawab, selalu **tambahkan satu detail** atau **bertanya balik** (*How about you? / What about you? / And you?*).

options: What kind of projects do you work on?
blocks.explain: What kind of projects… can't be answered with just yes or no, so the person has to say more. The other two are closed questions: 'Yes.' is a complete answer.

id.explain: What kind of projects… tidak bisa dijawab hanya dengan yes atau no, jadi orangnya harus bercerita lebih banyak. Dua lainnya pertanyaan tertutup: 'Yes.' sudah jawaban yang lengkap.

blocks.text:
**Safe** topics with someone you've just met: the **event**, **work in general** (what they do, their projects, how long they've been there), **travel**, **food**, **the city**, the **weather** and the **traffic**, **hobbies**, films and sport.

**Sensitive** topics (better to avoid with a new contact): **salary and money**, **age**, **weight and body**, **religion**, **politics**, **marriage and children**.

Why? It's a cultural difference, not good or bad manners. In Indonesia, questions like *Umurnya berapa?*, *Sudah nikah?*, *Kapan nikah?*, *Gajinya berapa di sana?* or *Gendutan, ya!* often show friendly attention: the person cares about you. In many English-speaking workplaces (the UK, the US, Australia, and many international offices), the same questions from someone new feel **intrusive**: too personal, as if the person is entering your private life. So you adapt to your listener, just as you choose formal words for a formal email.

These are **tendencies**, not laws. Close friends talk about everything, and if the other person brings a topic up first (*My wife and I just had a baby!*), you can follow it: *Congratulations! Boy or girl?*

id.text:
Topik **aman** dengan orang yang baru kamu kenal: **acaranya**, **pekerjaan secara umum** (apa pekerjaannya, proyeknya, sudah berapa lama di sana), **perjalanan**, **makanan**, **kotanya**, **cuaca** dan **macet**, **hobi**, film dan olahraga.

Topik **sensitif** (sebaiknya dihindari dengan kenalan baru): **gaji dan uang**, **umur**, **berat badan dan bentuk tubuh**, **agama**, **politik**, **pernikahan dan anak**.

Kenapa? Ini perbedaan budaya, bukan soal sopan atau tidak sopan. Di Indonesia, pertanyaan seperti *Umurnya berapa?*, *Sudah nikah?*, *Kapan nikah?*, *Gajinya berapa di sana?* atau *Gendutan, ya!* sering menunjukkan perhatian yang ramah: orang itu peduli padamu. Di banyak tempat kerja berbahasa Inggris (Inggris, Amerika, Australia, dan banyak kantor internasional), pertanyaan yang sama dari orang yang baru dikenal terasa **intrusive** (terlalu mencampuri): terlalu pribadi, seolah-olah orang itu masuk ke kehidupan pribadimu. Jadi kamu menyesuaikan diri dengan lawan bicaramu, sama seperti kamu memilih kata formal untuk email formal.

Ini **kecenderungan**, bukan hukum. Teman dekat bisa membicarakan apa saja, dan kalau lawan bicaramu sendiri yang membuka topiknya (*My wife and I just had a baby!*), kamu boleh mengikutinya: *Congratulations! Boy or girl?*

blocks.text: If someone asks **you** a sensitive question, you don't have to answer it. Smile, give a light answer and change the topic with **Anyway, …**: *How much do you earn? → Ha, enough to pay the bills! Anyway, how's the conference so far?* And if you meet someone from Indonesia who asks *Kapan nikah?*, now you know they probably just mean to be friendly.

id.text: Kalau seseorang menanyakan pertanyaan sensitif **kepadamu**, kamu tidak wajib menjawabnya. Tersenyum, beri jawaban ringan, lalu ganti topik dengan **Anyway, …** (ngomong-ngomong): *How much do you earn? → Ha, enough to pay the bills!* (cukup buat bayar tagihan) *Anyway, how's the conference so far?* Dan kalau ada orang Indonesia yang bertanya *Kapan nikah?*, sekarang kamu tahu dia mungkin hanya ingin ramah.

blocks.prompt: A new colleague from the UK says: 'I'm just back from two weeks in Japan!' Which reply is best?
options: Oh, nice! What was the best part?
How much did the trip cost you?
blocks.explain: Travel is a safe topic, and 'What was the best part?' is an open follow-up question. Comments about the body sound rude, and money questions feel too personal with a new colleague.

id.prompt: Rekan kerja baru dari Inggris berkata: 'I'm just back from two weeks in Japan!' Balasan mana yang paling baik?
id.explain: Perjalanan adalah topik aman, dan 'What was the best part?' adalah pertanyaan lanjutan yang terbuka. Komentar tentang tubuh terdengar kasar, dan pertanyaan soal uang terasa terlalu pribadi dengan rekan kerja baru.

material.title: Closing politely: leaving without walking away

blocks.text:
At a networking event, people move around, so ending a conversation is normal. Just do it politely. A good exit has three parts:
1. **Signal + a reason.** *Well, …* or *Anyway, …* tells the person the end is coming. Then: *I should let you go* (polite, because it's about **their** time: *aku nggak mau menyita waktumu*), *I'm going to get another coffee*, or *I need to find my colleague before the next session.*
2. **Something nice.** *It was great talking to you.* / *It was really nice meeting you.* (*Nice to meet you* is the greeting at the start; at the end, *It was nice meeting you* sounds more natural.)
3. **A next step.** *Let's keep in touch. Here's my card.* (a **business card** = kartu nama) / *Let's connect on LinkedIn.* / *Enjoy the rest of the conference!* / *Hope to see you at the next one.*

id.text:
Di networking event orang berpindah-pindah, jadi mengakhiri obrolan itu hal yang biasa. Lakukan saja dengan sopan. Penutup yang baik punya tiga bagian:
1. **Tanda + alasan.** *Well, …* atau *Anyway, …* memberi tahu bahwa obrolan akan selesai. Lalu: *I should let you go* (sopan, karena tentang waktu **dia**: *aku nggak mau menyita waktumu*), *I'm going to get another coffee* (aku mau ambil kopi lagi), atau *I need to find my colleague before the next session* (aku harus cari rekanku sebelum sesi berikutnya).
2. **Sesuatu yang menyenangkan.** *It was great talking to you.* / *It was really nice meeting you.* (*Nice to meet you* adalah sapaan di awal; di akhir, *It was nice meeting you* terdengar lebih alami.)
3. **Langkah berikutnya.** *Let's keep in touch. Here's my card.* (**business card** = kartu nama) / *Let's connect on LinkedIn.* / *Enjoy the rest of the conference!* / *Hope to see you at the next one.*

rows.en: Well, I should let you go. It was great talking to you.
rows.id: Yah, aku nggak mau menyita waktumu lagi. Senang sekali ngobrol denganmu.

rows.id: Ngomong-ngomong, aku harus cari rekanku sebelum sesi berikutnya.

rows.en: Let's keep in touch. Here's my card.

blocks.text: The Indonesian trap: *Saya duluan, ya* → *I go first* ✗. In English this doesn't mean you're leaving. Say **I should get going** or **I have to go now**. And don't just walk away in the middle of the conversation: in English that feels rude, even at a busy event.

id.text: Jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia: *Saya duluan, ya* → *I go first* ✗. Dalam bahasa Inggris ini tidak berarti kamu pamit pergi. Katakan **I should get going** atau **I have to go now**. Dan jangan langsung pergi di tengah obrolan: dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris itu terasa kasar, bahkan di acara yang ramai.

blocks.prompt: It was great ___ you. Let's keep in touch!
blocks.explain: The phrase to remember is It was great talking to you, with the -ing form. 'great talk to you' has no -ing, and 'to talking' puts the words in the wrong order.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: It was great ___ you. Let's keep in touch!
id.explain: Ungkapan yang perlu diingat adalah It was great talking to you, dengan bentuk -ing. 'great talk to you' tidak memakai -ing, dan 'to talking' urutannya salah.

id.title: Menutup dengan sopan: pamit tanpa langsung pergi

material.title: All together: a coffee break in Jakarta

blocks.text: Here's a whole conversation at a fintech conference. Notice the moves: an opener with a tag and a name, an open question, a detail plus a question back, showing interest, a follow-up, and a polite exit with a next step. Nobody asks about salary, age or marriage.

id.text: Ini satu obrolan lengkap di sebuah konferensi fintech. Perhatikan langkah-langkahnya: pembuka dengan tag dan nama, pertanyaan terbuka, satu detail plus bertanya balik, menunjukkan minat, pertanyaan lanjutan, dan penutup yang sopan dengan langkah berikutnya. Tidak ada yang menanyakan gaji, umur atau pernikahan.

rows.en: Sari: The coffee here is great, isn't it? I'm Sari, by the way.
rows.id: Sari: Kopinya enak, ya? Omong-omong, saya Sari.

rows.en: Mark: Hi, Sari, I'm Mark. Yes, much better than at most conferences!
rows.id: Mark: Hai, Sari, saya Mark. Iya, jauh lebih enak daripada di kebanyakan konferensi!

rows.en: Sari: So, what brings you to Jakarta, Mark?
rows.id: Sari: Jadi, apa yang membawamu ke Jakarta, Mark?

rows.en: Mark: My company is opening an office here. I'm in charge of the new team. How about you?
rows.id: Mark: Perusahaan saya membuka kantor di sini. Saya memimpin tim barunya. Kalau kamu?

rows.en: Sari: I work for a digital bank in Surabaya. Oh, a new team? That must be exciting!
rows.id: Sari: Saya kerja di sebuah bank digital di Surabaya. Oh, tim baru? Pasti seru, ya!

rows.en: Mark: It is! But the traffic here is something else.
rows.id: Mark: Iya! Tapi macet di sini luar biasa.

rows.en: Sari: Ha, you get used to it! Well, I should let you go. Let's connect on LinkedIn.
rows.id: Sari: Haha, nanti juga terbiasa! Yah, aku nggak mau menyita waktumu lagi. Yuk, terhubung di LinkedIn.

resources.title: Your guide to small talk topics, phrases and openers in English

resources.title: How to make small talk at work: What to say
resources.note: A video lesson, all in English, on small talk with colleagues you already know: catching up (What have you been up to?), reacting, and casual goodbyes. engVid marks it as advanced, and it adds informal phrases (Long time no see, Take it easy) that go beyond this lesson.

id.note: Video pelajaran, seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris, tentang small talk dengan rekan kerja yang sudah kamu kenal: bertukar kabar (What have you been up to?), bereaksi, dan cara pamit yang santai. engVid menandainya sebagai tingkat lanjut, dan video ini menambahkan ungkapan informal (Long time no see, Take it easy) di luar pelajaran ini.

id.intro: Hai! Di konferensi, saat coffee break atau di networking event, dua menit pertama small talk bisa membuka pintu ke pekerjaan, klien atau teman baru. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan memulai obrolan, menjaganya tetap berjalan, memilih topik yang aman, dan pamit dengan sopan. Pemanasan: kamu berdiri di samping orang yang belum kamu kenal saat coffee break. Apa kalimat pertama yang akan kamu ucapkan?
suggestedQuestions: Apa yang bisa aku katakan kalau seseorang menanyakan berapa gajiku?
Apakah 'Where do you live?' termasuk pertanyaan sensitif?
Bagaimana cara mengakhiri obrolan kalau lawan bicaraku terus bicara?
Apakah boleh mengatakan 'Nice to meet you' di akhir obrolan?

assessment.stn-1: Kamu ada di sebuah konferensi teknologi di Jakarta. Presentasi besar pertama (keynote) baru saja selesai, dan kamu ingin mulai mengobrol dengan orang di sebelahmu. Lengkapi pembuka ini dengan question tag (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'The keynote was really good, ___?'
assessment.stn-2: Di sebuah networking event di Bandung, kamu ingin bertanya dengan ramah kepada orang yang belum kamu kenal kenapa dia datang. Lengkapi dengan satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'So, what ___ you here?'
assessment.stn-3: Ubah pertanyaan tertutup (yes/no) ini menjadi pertanyaan terbuka dengan arti yang sama. Tulis satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'Do you like your job?' → 'What do you ___ most about your job?'
assessment.stn-4:
Rina bertemu Tom, seorang manajer dari Inggris, di sebuah networking event di Jakarta. Ini obrolan pertama mereka. Pertanyaan Rina yang mana yang sensitif? Tulis A, B atau C.
A: What do you think of Jakarta so far?
B: How much do you earn?
C: Have you tried the satay here?
assessment.stn-5: Kamu mengobrol dengan kenalan baru dari Kanada di sebuah konferensi di Singapura. Topik mana yang paling aman untuk small talk: religion, salary, travel atau weight? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.stn-6: Kamu sudah mengobrol sepuluh menit dengan seorang pembicara setelah presentasinya, dan kamu melihat orang lain menunggu untuk bicara dengannya. Lengkapi penutup yang sopan ini dengan satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'Well, I should let you ___. Thanks so much for your talk!'
assessment.stn-7: Di akhir obrolan yang menyenangkan dengan klien baru, kamu ingin tetap berhubungan. Lengkapi dengan satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'Let's keep in ___. Here's my card.'
